analysis.title: GS Garrett - weekend prep 15 Nov 2026
key_insights: Brian Garrett describes the cash market as lacking conviction. The themes that used to carry conviction are being challenged, with the AI theme singled out, and investors are reluctant to press a directional view into year end.

2026 has been a year of two halves. The first half had large returns (Korea +130%, SMH +80%, momentum pair +70%, AI winners +50%) and the NDX 2-month Sharpe ratio hit its highest level since the late 1990s in June. In the second half, themes now move on horizons of days or hours instead of 6 months.

The vol market is far more confident than the cash market that the early-November selloff was an isolated event. The SPX year-end straddle costs less than the index moved in a single session last Thursday.

Prime brokerage data shows risk reduction continuing. Hedge funds have sold US equities in 5 of the last 6 weeks, long selling outpaces short covering by 2.8 to 1, and net exposure is in the 2nd percentile of its 5-year range.
Globally, single stocks have been sold for 9 straight weeks while macro product has been bought for 4 straight weeks. Funds are selling longs and covering macro shorts.
Technology was the most net sold sector this week. The US info tech long/short ratio closed at the lowest level on record (2016 start) and sector exposure is at its lowest in a decade.
The OneDelta desk reports long-only supply of NVDA, with the dollars moving into hyperscalers and other megacap tech. Money is shifting within the largest companies, not leaving them.

GS futures models show vol-control and risk-parity funds unwinding SPX after last Thursday's extreme move. They estimate about $27bn of SPX supply over the next few sessions, and these funds re-risk only if vol keeps falling.

Demand is building in energy commodities after Brent fell about 20% in 7 sessions at the start of November, the sharpest drawdown outside Covid. Thursday's price and open interest action points to new longs entering through both futures and calls.
Index calls are not crowded. There has been almost no upside call chasing, and put/call skew has firmed on demand for downside protection.
Structuring: a 3-month ~5.5% OTM call can be fully funded by a ~10% OTM put (costless risk reversal). The 10% OTM put also funds 2x 3-month 108/118 call spreads for clients willing to cap the upside.
VIX downside after a selloff has replaced SPX upside as the favored trade. VIX puts have had more volume over the last 10 sessions than at any other point this year.
Implied minus realized vol is at its widest negative level in over a year and is negative in every US sector except utilities. The options market is treating the volatility spike as a one-off.
The NDX year-end straddle (6.8%) is only marginally more expensive than last Thursday's NDX move (-6.4%). The SPX year-end straddle (4.2%) is cheaper than last Thursday's move (-4.4%).

Baskets: 12m momentum (GSPRHIMO) has its best outperformance versus 3m momentum (GSPRHMO3) in GS records. More AI names now sit in the short leg of 3m momentum, positioning in momentum has collapsed, and the consensus winners are no longer crowded.
Retail participation is undaunted. The gap between US long/short net exposure (Wall Street) and AAII equity exposure (Main Street) is widening, with AAII data through 31 Oct.

The note links GS's 2027 outlooks. Hatzius forecasts 2.8% global growth in 2027 with downside risks from Iran escalation, fiscal deficits and weaker AI spending. Dom Wilson lists 10 market themes including a maturing cycle, an AI impulse peaking, and bonds reclaiming macro and hedging value.

tension_points.bull_case: Options are pricing the early-November vol spike as a one-off. Implied minus realized vol is at its widest negative level in over a year and is negative in every US sector except utilities. Index calls are not crowded, so a rebound has room to run.
tension_points.bear_case: Cash positioning is defensive. Hedge funds have sold US equities in 5 of the last 6 weeks, net exposure is in the 2nd percentile, and vol-control funds are unwinding about $27bn of SPX. The SPX year-end straddle (4.2%) costs less than last Thursday's single-session move (-4.4%).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another single-session SPX move the size of last Thursday's -4.4%, which exceeds the 4.2% the year-end straddle prices.
